rv.q: But the play’s slight excesses can easily be forgiven, especially since women’s experience seems to have evaporated almost entirely from movie screens as a subject worthy of illumination through entertainment.
Neither Terrence McNally’s mishmash of a book nor the sometimes syrupy songs (by Lynn Ahrens and Stephen Flaherty) do the show any favors.
Sarah Ruhl's 'In the Next Room (or the Vibrator Play)' is a thoughtful, funny and surprisingly tender exploration
Who knew the two could be linked so satisfactorily on stage?
Sarah Ruhl's frank, funny and unexpectedly touching new play about Victorian sexuality and emotional intimacy opens with a scene that might have been lifted from a medical textbook of the 1880s.
Performances are beautifully detailed, resisting caricature for psychological realism even in the funniest situations.
Hate to be a buzz kill, but the play fakes its climax.
Sweet. But it's too lite to be illuminating.
